media.vs_qualified_file: 15,150,646 bytes; same 449 pictures and same 29.97 fps content, roughly 2.3 times the bitrate

user_report: Played the bigger file once; reports it played a lot slower.
boot_state: no power cycle; syslog still shows the single 07:41:02 UTC boot, so this run followed the entry 575 cold run on the same uptime

outcome.note: the file still plays correctly and completely with zero error flags; it is throttled, not corrupted

helper_log.would_block_placement: all 384 carry submitted=0 and precede the first byte; after read event 1 the log records none, so the helper always had data ready and the parent never saw EAGAIN during steady delivery

measurement.curve_shape: flat at the ceiling for the entire session, with no burst-then-decay, because demand exceeds supply throughout

correction_to_entry_572.superseded_claim: entry 572 concluded that raising the four-chunk per-poll budget in mediaplayer_poll() would not correct anything because steady throughput was never the limiting quantity, and listed that candidate as ruled out
correction_to_entry_572.correction: that conclusion holds only for the 8 Mbps qualified file, whose 1,010,157 B/s demand sits below the ceiling. It is false in general. For any stream above roughly 1.41 MB/s the per-poll budget is the binding constraint and is precisely what throttles playback.
correction_to_entry_572.evidence: the big file's delivery rate matches 4 x 4096 x 86.2 Hz to 0.01 percent, and its frame-rate deficit matches its delivery deficit to 0.2 percent

project_level_implication.concern: the delivery ceiling of about 1.41 MB/s is marginal for the project's stated long-term goal of commercial DVD playback
project_level_implication.figures: DVD peak video bitrate is 9.8 Mbps or about 1.225 MB/s, and a full program stream may reach 10.08 Mbps or about 1.26 MB/s, leaving roughly 12 percent headroom against the measured ceiling
project_level_implication.note: startup dead time already consumes more margin than that, so peak-rate DVD titles would be at risk on the current delivery path even before considering audio demultiplexing

scope_limitations: This is one run of the larger file and it was not preceded by a power cycle.
The 86.2 Hz poll rate is inferred from read counts and elapsed time rather than measured inside MiSTer main, though it now agrees across two files with very different demands.
Only three of the 188 deadline records are retained by the snapshot, at ordinals 7, 8 and 9.
Whether raising the per-poll budget is safe with respect to MiSTer main's other responsibilities has not been assessed and is not proposed here.
The DVD bitrate figures are standard maxima and are not measurements of any particular title.
